title: The DOM and events
intro: JavaScript can do more than calculate values: it can read and change the page the user sees. In this lesson, you will learn how the browser represents HTML as the DOM, how to respond to user events, and how to build a small interactive to-do list safely.
takeaways: The DOM is the browser's object representation of the HTML document, and JavaScript can use it to find and modify elements.
Use querySelector and querySelectorAll to find elements, classList for classes, and createElement or remove for dynamic DOM changes.
addEventListener lets your code respond to clicks, input, form submissions, keyboard events, and other browser events.
Event delegation lets one parent handler manage dynamically created child elements, while preventDefault stops an event's default browser action.
Use textContent for user-provided text and treat innerHTML as potentially dangerous when its content is not trusted.

quiz.question: What does `document.querySelector("#todo-input")` return?
options: Every element with the todo-input ID
The first element matching the selector, or null if there is no match
An array of all input elements
The text inside the input
quiz.explanation: querySelector returns the first matching element. If nothing matches the selector, it returns null.

quiz.question: Which method toggles a CSS class on an element?
options: classList.toggle()
class.toggle()
style.toggle()
toggleClassList()
quiz.explanation: classList.toggle() adds the class when it is missing and removes it when it is already present.

quiz.question: What does `event.preventDefault()` do in a form submit handler?
options: Deletes the form
Stops JavaScript from running
Prevents the event's default browser action
Prevents all future events on the form
quiz.explanation: For a form submission, preventDefault() can stop the browser's normal submission behaviour so JavaScript can handle the form itself.

quiz.question: Why is `textContent` generally safer than assigning user input to `innerHTML`?
options: textContent automatically converts text to CSS
textContent is always faster
textContent only works with forms
textContent treats the value as text instead of interpreting it as HTML
quiz.explanation: textContent inserts plain text. innerHTML parses its value as HTML, which can create an XSS risk when the value contains untrusted user input.

quiz.question: What does the `defer` attribute do for an external script in the document head?
options: Prevents the script from ever running
Delays execution until the HTML document has been parsed
Converts JavaScript into TypeScript
Runs the script before the HTML is parsed
quiz.explanation: A deferred external script can download while the document is parsed but executes after parsing has completed, making DOM elements available.

exercise.title: Build a mini to-do list
exercise.task: Build a complete HTML page containing a form with the exact ID `todo-form`, an input with the exact ID `todo-input`, a submit button, an empty `ul` with the exact ID `todo-list`, and a paragraph with the exact ID `todo-count`. Submitting the form must add an `li` containing the trimmed input text using `textContent`, clear the input, ignore empty or whitespace-only input, and update the counter so it starts as `0 tasks` and becomes `1 task`, `2 tasks`, and so on. Clicking an `li` must toggle the class `done`, and the implementation must work for items added after the page loads. The tests use `typeInto` on `#todo-input` and submit the form with `requestSubmit()` or by clicking the submit button, so keep these exact selectors and use a real form submission handler.
exercise.starter: 0 tasks
exercise.solution: 0 tasks
exercise.hint: Select the form, input, list, and counter with their required IDs. In the submit handler, call preventDefault(), trim the input value, return early for an empty string, create an li with createElement(), set its textContent, append it, clear the input, and update the counter. Attach one click handler to the ul and use event delegation with event.target.matches("li") to toggle the done class.

tests.name: Starts with an empty list and zero tasks
tests.code: const list = document.querySelector("#todo-list"); const count = document.querySelector("#todo-count"); return list.children.length === 0 && count.textContent.trim() === "0 tasks";

tests.name: Adds a trimmed task
tests.code: const input = document.querySelector("#todo-input"); const form = document.querySelector("#todo-form"); input.value = "  Buy milk  "; form.requestSubmit(); await tick(); const item = document.querySelector("#todo-list li"); return item && item.textContent === "Buy milk" && input.value === "" && document.querySelector("#todo-count").textContent.trim() === "1 task";

tests.name: Ignores empty input
tests.code: const input = document.querySelector("#todo-input"); const form = document.querySelector("#todo-form"); input.value = "   "; form.requestSubmit(); await tick(); return document.querySelectorAll("#todo-list li").length === 0 && document.querySelector("#todo-count").textContent.trim() === "0 tasks";

tests.name: Updates the plural task count
tests.code: const input = document.querySelector("#todo-input"); const form = document.querySelector("#todo-form"); input.value = "First"; form.requestSubmit(); await tick(); input.value = "Second"; form.requestSubmit(); await tick(); return document.querySelectorAll("#todo-list li").length === 2 && document.querySelector("#todo-count").textContent.trim() === "2 tasks";

tests.name: Toggles the done class when an item is clicked
tests.code: const input = document.querySelector("#todo-input"); const form = document.querySelector("#todo-form"); input.value = "Finish lesson"; form.requestSubmit(); await tick(); const item = document.querySelector("#todo-list li"); await click(item); const afterFirstClick = item.classList.contains("done"); await click(item); const afterSecondClick = item.classList.contains("done"); return afterFirstClick === true && afterSecondClick === false;

tests.name: Inserts user text as text content
tests.code: const input = document.querySelector("#todo-input"); const form = document.querySelector("#todo-form"); input.value = "Safe text"; form.requestSubmit(); await tick(); const item = document.querySelector("#todo-list li"); return item && item.textContent === "Safe text" && item.querySelector("strong") === null;
